description: You are a medical oncologist at a urology-oncology combined clinic. A 78-year-old patient with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer is being initiated on abiraterone acetate. He has significant comorbidities requiring several co-medications from other specialties: ketoconazole (prescribed by dermatology for a resistant fungal skin infection, given that topical therapies have failed), warfarin (prescribed by cardiology for a mechanical heart valve prosthesis requiring anticoagulation), and acenocoumarol (newly prescribed by the haematology team as part of a DVT treatment protocol). Before initiating abiraterone, you must use the Liverpool Cancer iChart Archive app to screen all three co-medications for potential interactions. After reviewing all three interaction ratings, navigate to and remain on the Interaction Details screen for the co-medication that carries the most clinically significant contraindication with abiraterone.

metadata.expected_mechanism: Combined CYP17A1 inhibition — dual blockade of androgen synthesis pathway
metadata.clinical_context: mCRPC patient on abiraterone with polypharmacy needing safety review
